title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: In an agent run, the model's call at step 3 gives an answer that uses a calendar result fetched during step 2. How does the model have that result at step 3?

options.text: It kept the result in its own memory after the step 2 call
The program included the result in the context it sent for step 3
It looked the result up again in the booking system by itself
The booking system pushed the result to it between the two calls

items.stem: An assistant run makes three model calls. The system prompt and tool descriptions are 2,000 tokens and the question is 100 tokens. After call 1, a manual search adds 5,000 tokens to the context. After call 2, a calendar check adds 400 tokens. Call 3 writes the final answer. Ignore the model's own short outputs. How many tokens does the model read in total across the three calls?
A teammate wants to paste all twelve machine manuals (about 400,000 tokens) into the system prompt, because the chosen model has a 1,000,000-token window. What is the best objection?

options.text: It will not fit, because a system prompt is capped well below the window
It is fine, since anything that fits in the window costs the same to use
Every call re-reads and pays for all of it, and accuracy can suffer
The model would only read the first manual and ignore the other eleven

items.stem: A student's session ends. A week later the same student opens a new session. In one or two sentences, what must the program do at the start of the new session for the assistant to know the student's training status, and why?
Which one of these facts is best saved as a note to be read at the start of a later session, rather than kept in the system prompt or fetched by manual search?

options.text: Dana asked to get booking reminders by email, not by text message
The laser cutter's focus procedure is described on page 14 of its manual
Every answer about a machine must name the manual section it used
The 3D printer is booked from 2 pm to 4 pm on this coming Friday
